text: Debugging is a crucial skill for any programmer. When a program doesn’t work, the first step is identifying the bug. This means carefully reading error messages and checking where the code behaves unexpectedly. A systematic approach is essential: instead of guessing, you should break the problem into smaller parts and test each one. Using debugging tools, like breakpoints in an IDE, helps you pause the program and inspect values. Additionally, logging—printing messages to the console—shows what happens step by step. By combining these methods, you can find and fix errors more quickly and avoid frustration.
